extracted.intended_audience: Prospective Coursera learners: aspiring short-story writers to established novelists (beginner-to-college-level)
extracted.subtask_description: An online specialization for learners who want to craft original short stories, narrative essays, or memoirs through instruction on plot, character, setting, and style, plus peer review and a capstone project. Courses are college-level but accessible to advanced high-school students.

rubrics_metrics.name: Craft an original story that absorbs a reader
rubrics_metrics.description: Craft an original story that will absorb a reader’s interest from the beginning to end.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is the program-level learning outcome and the overarching standard for the Capstone: the finished piece should hold reader interest throughout.

rubrics_metrics.name: Master techniques to compose a bracing story with memorable characters and interesting setting
rubrics_metrics.description: You will master the techniques that good writers use to compose a bracing story, populated with memorable characters in an interesting setting, written in a fresh descriptive style.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Emphasis on combining plot, character, setting, and style into a cohesive, engaging piece; stylistic freshness and descriptive strength are highlighted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Analyze and constructively evaluate peer writing
rubrics_metrics.description: You will analyze and constructively evaluate peer writing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Peer-review skill is an explicit learning objective: learners should be able to give and receive constructive critiques as part of improving their own and others' work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Capstone: draft, rewrite, and complete a substantial original story in chosen genre
rubrics_metrics.description: In the Capstone, you will draft, rewrite, and complete a substantial original story in the genre of your choosing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Capstone requires multiple drafting and revision cycles; successful completion demonstrates integration of the courses' techniques.

rubrics_metrics.name: Plot: outline, structure, narrative arc, pacing, reversals, and coherence
rubrics_metrics.description: Learn how to outline and structure a plot, discuss narrative arc, pacing and reversals and reveal the inevitable surprise: connecting the beginning, middle and end.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Focus on what keeps a story moving and how plot manipulates reader feelings, expectations, and desires; instruction includes outlining and structuring techniques to ensure a coherent arc and satisfying connections across story parts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Character: build complex, vivid, unforgettable characters with inner and outer lives
rubrics_metrics.description: Discover how to build and bring to life complex, vivid and unforgettable characters. Develop inner (thoughts and feelings) and outer (appearance, habits, behavior) lives for characters.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes written exercises, use (and cautions about use) of personal life experiences, techniques to let characters surprise the writer, and attention to how character detail leads to richer stories.

rubrics_metrics.name: Setting and Description: ground story in a concrete world with sharp sensory detail and credibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Learn the techniques that masters of fiction use to ground a story in a concrete world; learn how to describe the physical world in sharp, sensory detail and how to build credibility through research.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Also uses creative meditation exercises to deepen the writer's understanding of story worlds so readers can 'see all that we imagine.' Emphasizes sensory specificity and researched plausibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Style: metaphor, imagery, clarity, grace, inventiveness, and revision skills
rubrics_metrics.description: Study the use of metaphor and imagery, and demonstrate how clarity, grace, and inventiveness in word choice are imperative to a story’s success. Writers will emerge with the revision skills essential to good prose.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Frames style as something a writer can choose and develop; includes practical revision techniques and attention to precise, inventive language (the 'art of putting pressure on written language').

rubrics_metrics.name: Capstone format and length requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Draft a complete story, narrative essay, or memoir of 8–15 pages.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Capstone must be a finished piece in one of the specified genres and within the stated page-length range; completion includes revision informed by peer feedback and learning the professional steps to publish or present work publicly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Revision practice and writerly habits
rubrics_metrics.description: Learn the patient habits of revision that make up the writer’s life; revise, rewrite, and complete work with advice of peer readers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Emphasizes sustained revision practices, iterative drafts, and collaborative feedback as central evaluative standards for producing publishable work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Course rigor and accessibility expectation
rubrics_metrics.description: The Specialization courses will be rigorous and taught at the college level, but will be accessible to advanced high school students as well.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sets expectations for the level of challenge and prior background needed; implies evaluation standards aligned with college-level instruction while being accessible to motivated beginners.
